network_intro: Uplinks besides WiFi. Each change is verified and waits for your confirmation.
netview_intro: Read-only. Change interfaces and firewall zones in LuCI.
netview_partial: The firewall could not be read; zones are missing.
netview_zones_unavailable: Could not read the firewall zones.
netview_restart_body: The uplink goes down and comes back up; internet access pauses for a few seconds. Settings stay as they are.
netview_restart_not_up: {name} was restarted but is not up after 30 seconds.
netview_restart_lockout_title: You may lose access to the router
netview_restart_lockout_body: Your WiFi access point shares its radio with the WiFi uplink and drops for a few seconds during the restart. Reconnect to it afterwards.
netview_restart_err_pending: A change is waiting for confirmation; confirm or roll it back first.
netview_restart_err_busy: Another restart or change is in progress; try again shortly.
netview_restart_err_failed: The restart failed. Try again; the router reports the failure until then.
netview_restart_err_unavailable: The interface could not be restarted.
diag_intro: Test from the router: ping a host, trace the route to it, or look up a name through the router's DNS (what your devices get).
diag_truncated: The output was cut at 16 KiB.
diag_err_target: Enter a host name or an IP address.
diag_err_busy: Another diagnostic is running; try again when it finishes.
diag_err_rate: Too many runs; wait a minute.
wol_intro: Wake a sleeping wired device by its MAC address. The device must have Wake-on-LAN turned on.
wol_err_mac: Enter a device MAC address like aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff.
wol_err_interface: That network is not available for Wake-on-LAN.
wol_err_busy: Another wake request is running; try again.
wol_err_rate: Too many wake requests; wait a minute.
wol_err_failed: Could not send the wake packet.
dhcp_intro: Hands out addresses on the LAN. Changes apply to new leases and renewals; current leases run on until they expire.
dhcp_off: The DHCP server is off: devices need a static address.
dhcp_confirm: New leases and renewals use the new settings. A device whose address leaves the pool gets a new one on its next renewal.
dhcp_confirm_off: Devices lose their address when their lease expires and new devices get none.
dhcp_confirm_off_caller: This device got its address from the router: it loses the connection when its lease expires unless you set a static address.
dhcp_err_invalid: The router refused these values; check the pool fits the LAN subnet.
dhcp_err_foreign: The DHCP settings were changed in a way Travo does not edit; use LuCI.
dhcp_err_busy: Another change is staged; try again.
dhcp_err_failed: Could not change the DHCP settings.
wan_intro: How the router gets Internet over the WAN port. A change is guarded: keep it within the confirm window or it rolls back.
wan_confirm: The WAN connection restarts. If the router's uplink route is lost, the change rolls back; otherwise keep it within the confirm window.
wan_rollback_failed: Rolling back the WAN settings failed; check the router.
wan_no_change: The WAN already has these settings.
wan_err_invalid: Check the address, gateway, DNS servers or PPPoE fields.
wan_err_overlaps_lan: The WAN subnet overlaps the LAN or guest network; pick another address.
wan_err_foreign: The WAN is configured in a way Travo does not edit; use LuCI.
wan_failed: Could not change the WAN settings.
lan_intro: The router's own address on the LAN. Changing it moves every device to a new subnet: you confirm the change from the new address, or it rolls back.
lan_confirm_title: Move the router to a new address?
lan_confirm: This page loses the connection. Reconnect this device (turn WiFi off and on, or unplug and replug the cable), open {url}, log in and keep the change within 3 minutes. Otherwise the router returns to {old}.
lan_moving: Reconnect this device (WiFi off and on, or replug the cable), then open the new address, log in and keep the change. Time left: {seconds} s.
lan_moving_fallback: If the new address does not load, the change rolls back and the router stays at {old}.
lan_moving_over: The confirm window has closed. Unless you kept the change at the new address, the router is back at {old}: reconnect this device and reload this page.
lan_pending: The router moved to {address}. Keep the change to finish, or roll back.
lan_confirmed: New LAN address kept. If Tailscale advertised the LAN, turn on advertising the LAN again in the Tailscale settings so it advertises the new subnet.
lan_rollback_failed: Rolling back the LAN address failed; check the router.
lan_no_change: The router already has this address.
lan_err_invalid: Enter a private IPv4 address with a /24 to /30 prefix, e.g. 192.168.8.1/24.
lan_err_overlap: The new subnet overlaps another network (guest, uplink or VPN); pick another one.
lan_err_pool: The DHCP pool does not fit the new subnet; shrink it first.
lan_err_dependents: Reservations, local DNS names or port forwards point outside the new subnet; change or remove them first.
lan_err_foreign: The LAN is configured in a way Travo does not edit; use LuCI.
lan_err_adguard_expert: AdGuard Home answers DNS on the current LAN address (expert topology). Switch AdGuard Home back to the default DNS topology first, then change the LAN address.
lan_failed: Could not change the LAN address.
port_forwards_intro: Make a device on the LAN reachable from the uplink side (WAN port or upstream WiFi). A change is guarded: keep it within the confirm window or it rolls back.
port_forwards_note: Ports are 1-65535 or a range like 8000-8010. The target must be a LAN device, never the router: its admin pages stay reachable from the LAN only.
port_forwards_add_body: Anyone on the uplink network can reach {target} on this port. The firewall reloads; keep the change within the confirm window.
port_forwards_remove_body: The device is no longer reachable from the uplink side on this port.
port_forwards_rolled_back: The port forward change was rolled back.
port_forwards_rollback_failed: Rolling back the port forward change failed; check the router.
port_forwards_failed: Could not change the port forwards.
port_forwards_err_invalid: Check the ports and the LAN device address (a LAN host, not the router).
port_forwards_err_in_use: Another enabled forward already uses that external port.
port_forwards_err_no_zone: The firewall has no wan or lan zone; use LuCI.
port_forwards_err_foreign: This forward was not created by Travo; edit it in LuCI.
dns_names_intro: Names the router answers for devices on your networks, like nas → 192.168.1.20. Upstream DNS, AdGuard and the VPN are not involved.
dns_names_remove_body: Devices can no longer reach it by this name.
dns_names_err_exists: That name already has a local DNS entry.
dns_names_err_foreign: That entry was set in LuCI; edit it there.
dns_names_err_input: Enter a host name and an IPv4 or IPv6 address.
usbtether_bound_missing: The phone on {device} is not connected. Plug it in, or use the phone that is connected now.
usbtether_no_phone: Install the drivers, connect a phone by USB, then turn on USB tethering (Android) or Personal Hotspot (iPhone).
usbtether_iphone_hint: Unlock the iPhone, tap Trust, and turn on Personal Hotspot (Allow Others to Join) before enabling.
usbtether_enable_help: The phone joins the internet uplinks behind Ethernet and WiFi: it carries traffic while they have no connection. Confirm the change once the phone link is up.
usbtether_disable_help: If the phone is your only uplink, the router and its clients lose internet.
usbtether_drivers_help: Installing downloads packages over the current uplink and uses router flash.
usbtether_drivers_no_space: Not enough free flash for the drivers.
usbtether_drivers_busy: A driver install is already running.
usbtether_drivers_failed: The driver install did not finish. Check the uplink and install again.
usbtether_ambiguous: More than one phone is connected; choose one.
usbtether_unsupported: The firewall layout is not supported: the wan zone must list its networks.
usbtether_no_change: The USB uplink is already in that state.
usbtether_rolled_back: The USB uplink did not come up; the previous settings are back.
usbtether_rollback_failed: Restoring the previous uplink settings failed. Check the router.
failover_help: Traffic uses the first uplink in the list that is up and moves to the next when it goes down. IPv4 only; IPv6 keeps the normal route.
failover_install_note: Enabling installs the mwan3 package over the current uplink.
failover_enable_help: Priority: {order}. The change is verified with a real connection test and waits for your confirmation.
failover_disable_help: Traffic goes back to the normal default route. The failover settings stay for the next time.
failover_busy: A failover change is still running.
failover_disable_failed: Failover could not be disabled. Try again.
failover_offline: The router needs a working internet connection to verify failover.
failover_conflict: An existing mwan3 section uses a name failover needs. Remove it in LuCI first.
failover_tailscale_conflict: Tailscale is running or starts at boot and cannot share the router with failover yet. Stop it and turn off its autostart, or remove Tailscale, first.
failover_invalid: Choose two or three different uplinks.
failover_failed: Failover could not be enabled. Enabling again retries it.
failover_rolled_back: Failover did not verify; the previous settings are back.
failover_rolled_back_reason: Failover did not verify: {reason}. The previous settings are back.
failover_check_config: the mwan3 settings did not read back as saved
failover_check_tracking: an uplink was not tracked online
failover_check_hook: mwan3 could not hook into the firewall
failover_check_first_rule: another mwan3 rule matched before failover
failover_check_policy_mark: traffic was not sent to the first uplink
failover_same_subnet: Two of the chosen uplinks are in the same network (for example cable and WiFi to the same router). Failover cannot keep the backup working when the first one fails; choose uplinks from different networks.
failover_mangle_incompatible: The router's firewall holds rules failover cannot work with (left by another tool). Remove them, then enable failover again.
failover_rollback_failed: Restoring the previous failover settings failed. Check the router.
failover_warning_adopted: mwan3 section {section} was taken over: its tracking options were replaced.
failover_warning_edited: mwan3 section {section} was edited by hand and is overwritten.
failover_warning_stale: mwan3 section {section} was edited by hand and is kept, unused.
captive_login_needed: This network asks you to sign in before it lets you online.
captive_offline_hint: The uplink is connected, but the internet is not reachable. A hotel login page may need the hotel's DNS.
captive_dns_active: Hotel DNS in use: DNS filtering and VPN DNS are paused.
captive_dns_pending: A DNS change did not finish. DNS may still point at the hotel.
captive_error_no_uplink_dns: The uplink did not provide a DNS server.
captive_error_pending: A DNS change did not finish; it must be retried first.
captive_error_foreign_staged: DNS settings have unsaved changes from another tool, such as LuCI.
captive_renew_blocked: An earlier renew could not prove the uplink came back.
captive_renew_done: Lease renewed. Open the hotel login again.
captive_error_renew_not_applicable: Renewing applies only to a WiFi uplink without internet.
captive_error_renew_unproven: The uplink did not come back within 10 seconds after the renew.
captive_accept_online: Logged in. The router is online.
captive_accept_needs_user: This login asks for your details, such as a room number. Open the hotel login.
captive_accept_no_form: The login page has nothing to accept automatically. Open the hotel login.
captive_accept_failed: The automatic login did not get online. Open the hotel login, or use hotel DNS first.
captive_error_accept_not_captive: No hotel login is detected right now.
captive_error_accept_busy: An automatic login is already running.
setup_body: Choose the root password for this router. You will use it to sign in.
setup_already_set: A password is already set on this router.
password_rules: Use 8 to 128 bytes, without line breaks.
rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
device_unavailable: The router is not responding. Try again.
system_backup_failed: Could not download the configuration backup.
reboot_confirm: The interface is unreachable for about a minute. Active sessions end.
reboot_timeout: The router did not come back within 3 minutes. Check power and the Ethernet cable, then reload this page.

match.key=txn: Confirm or roll back the pending change first.
match.key=pending: A restart is already in progress.

update_deferred: An automatic check was attempted within the last 24 hours.
update_rate_limited: The release source is limiting requests.
update_verify_failed: Could not verify the release package.
update_confirm: The interface briefly disconnects while the update installs.
update_applying: Installing update. Sign in again if prompted after restart.
update_rolled_back: Update failed. The previous version was restored.
update_apply_failed: Could not start the update operation.
vpn_kill_on_help: LAN devices reach the internet only through the tunnel. While the tunnel is down or off, they have no internet.
vpn_kill_off_help: If the tunnel drops, LAN devices fall back to the uplink.
vpn_kill_rollback_failed: Firewall restore failed. Check the router before trying again.
vpn_kill_not_connected: Connect the tunnel before enabling the kill switch.
vpn_kill_unsupported: This firewall layout is not supported for the kill switch.
vpn_kill_no_change: The kill switch is already in that state.
vpn_kill_failed: Could not change the kill switch.
vpn_split_full: Full tunnel: all traffic uses the VPN
vpn_split_routes: Routes through the VPN (IPv4 prefixes, one per line)
vpn_split_help: Leave empty for a full tunnel. The profile's DNS servers are routed through the VPN automatically. With the kill switch on, LAN devices reach only these routes.
vpn_split_invalid: Enter up to 32 distinct IPv4 prefixes such as 10.0.0.0/8, without 0.0.0.0/0.
vpn_split_profile_required: Select and apply a WireGuard profile first.
vpn_split_no_change: Split tunnel routes are already up to date.
vpn_split_failed: Could not change the split tunnel.
vpn_dns_verifying: Resolving a test name through the router…
vpn_dns_verify_ok: Resolution works through the tunnel resolvers
vpn_dns_verify_overridden: Another DNS layer is in charge
vpn_dns_verify_mismatch: Router DNS does not match the tunnel resolvers
vpn_invalid: Check the profile name and WireGuard configuration.
vpn_limit: You can save up to 32 profiles.
vpn_save_failed: Could not save the profile change. Try again.
vpn_tunnel_applying: Applying tunnel settings. An idle peer may need keepalive or tunnel traffic.
vpn_tunnel_rollback_failed: Tunnel restore failed. Check the router before trying again.
vpn_tunnel_unknown_result: The transaction result is unavailable. Check the tunnel status.
vpn_tunnel_no_change: Tunnel settings are already up to date.
vpn_tunnel_failed: Could not apply the tunnel change.
wifi_scanning: Scanning, this can take several seconds
wifi_scan_failed: No radio could complete the scan. Try again.
wifi_join_connecting: Connecting to {ssid}, this can take up to 30 seconds
wifi_join_rollback_failed: Rollback failed. Use Ethernet or the console.
wifi_join_no_free_radio: No free radio supports this network.
wifi_join_invalid_key: Enter a WiFi password with 8–63 printable ASCII characters.
wifi_join_not_found: This network was not found in the latest scan.
wifi_join_lockout: This change would disconnect you from the router.
wifi_join_no_change: This WiFi configuration is already in use.
wifi_join_unavailable: Could not verify the WiFi change.
wifi_saved_empty: No saved uplinks. Save one from a nearby network.
wifi_saved_unavailable: Saved uplinks are unavailable. Try again.
wifi_saved_forget_connected: This is the current uplink. Forgetting it keeps the current connection up.
wifi_saved_not_found: This saved uplink no longer exists.
wifi_saved_order_changed: Saved uplinks changed. Reload and try again.
wifi_reconnect_exhausted: Uplink lost. Automatic reconnect stopped after {attempts} attempts.
wifi_reconnect_suggest: {ssid} is a saved uplink in range.
wifi_reconnect_scan_hint: Scan to find a saved uplink in range.
wifi_reconnect_none_in_range: No saved uplink is in range.
wifi_save_limit: You can save up to 32 uplinks.
adguard_absent_body: AdGuard Home installs automatically after the first Internet connection. You can also install it now.
adguard_fail_open_body: DNS now uses the uplink resolver, without ad blocking. It switches back after AdGuard Home has answered for 10 minutes.
adguard_err_offline: AdGuard Home installs once the router has Internet.
adguard_err_no_space: Not enough free flash for AdGuard Home.
adguard_err_not_answering: AdGuard Home is not resolving yet. DNS stays at the uplink resolver.
adguard_err_busy: Another change is in progress. Try again shortly.
adguard_err_config: The AdGuard Home config has an unexpected format; Travo left it unchanged.
adguard_migration_failed: Moving AdGuard Home to loopback failed and was undone; Travo retries in an hour or after the config changes.
adguard_err_failed: The change failed. See the system log.
adguard_err_expert_topology: AdGuard Home answers DNS on port 53 (expert). Switch back to the default DNS setup first.
adguard_topology_intro: AdGuard Home answers every device directly and sees each client's address; the router's own DNS moves behind it and keeps VPN, captive portal and Tailscale DNS working. If AdGuard Home stops answering, DNS is down for up to a minute until Travo switches back by itself.
adguard_topology_confirm_on: DNS restarts for every device. Check that a website still opens, then keep the change; otherwise it is undone by itself. Afterwards an AdGuard Home outage is a short DNS outage for the whole network.
adguard_topology_confirm_off_title: Back to the default DNS setup?
adguard_topology_confirm_off: DNS restarts for every device. Check that a website still opens, then keep the change; otherwise it is undone by itself.
adguard_topology_rollback_failed: Restoring the DNS setup failed. See the system log.
adguard_topology_no_change: AdGuard Home already uses this setup.
adguard_topology_not_ready: AdGuard Home must be installed, running and on loopback first.
adguard_topology_foreign: The LAN or DHCP configuration has a shape Travo does not change.
wifi_join_moves_ap: This network needs the radio of {ssid}. That access point moves to the other radio; devices on it reconnect.
wifi_ap_key_hint: Leave empty to keep the current password.
wifi_schedule_zone: Times are the router's local time ({zone}), set under System settings.
wifi_schedule_local: Times are the router's local time, set under System settings.
wifi_schedule_cron_stopped: The router's cron service is not running; no rule fires.
wifi_schedule_empty: No schedule. Access points stay as they are.
wifi_schedule_delete_body: {ssid} is no longer turned off and on by this rule. Its current state stays.
wifi_schedule_hint: Both times apply on each selected day. An off time after the on time spans the night.
wifi_schedule_err_same: Off and on times must differ.
wifi_schedule_err_invalid: The router refused this schedule. Check the times and days.
wifi_schedule_err_ap: That access point no longer exists. Reload and pick another.
wifi_schedule_lockout_title: This schedule can lock you out
wifi_schedule_lockout_body: {ssid} is the only non-guest access point. When the schedule turns it off, devices on it, possibly including yours, lose the admin page until the on time or a cable connection.
wifi_ap_applying: Applying {ssid}, this can take up to 30 seconds
wifi_ap_radio_in_use: This radio carries the uplink. Move the uplink first.
wifi_ap_not_found: This access point no longer exists.
wifi_ssid_invalid: Enter a network name of 1–32 bytes.
wifi_guest_hint: Separate network {subnet} with internet only: no access to your devices or this router.
wifi_guest_overlap: The guest subnet overlaps another network.
wifi_guest_conflict: An existing guest configuration is not managed here.
wifi_mac_clone_unavailable: The router does not know this device's MAC. Connect directly and try again.
tokens_intro: Tokens let scripts and home automation call the API from the LAN with an Authorization: Bearer header. A read token can only read status; an admin token can change settings.
tokens_scope_read_hint: Read status only. Never changes anything and never reads secrets.
tokens_scope_admin_hint: Full control like a signed-in admin, except tokens, password and sessions.
tokens_secret_once: This token will not be shown again. Store it now; if you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.
tokens_copy_failed: Could not copy. Select the token and copy it by hand.
tokens_revoke_body: Anything using this token loses access immediately. This cannot be undone.
tokens_revoked: Revoked {name}. Anything using it has lost access.
tokens_err_limit: The token limit (16) is reached. Revoke a token first.
tokens_err_invalid: Enter a name of 1 to 256 characters.
tokens_err_session: Tokens can only be managed from a signed-in browser session.
tokens_err_failed: Could not change API tokens. Try again.
txn_pending_countdown: It rolls back automatically in {seconds} s unless you confirm.
wifi_lockout_title: You may lose access to the router
wifi_lockout_body: This change turns off the WiFi you are connected through. If you cannot reach the router afterwards, nothing confirms the change and it rolls back automatically.
wifi_ap_disable_body: Devices connected to {ssid} lose WiFi until you enable it again.
wifi_saved_forget_body: The saved password is removed from the router.
vpn_tunnel_disable_body: LAN traffic leaves through the uplink without the VPN. With the kill switch on, LAN devices have no internet.
vpn_delete_body: The WireGuard profile and its keys are removed from the router.
vpn_profile_selected: Profile {name} selected. Apply it from the tunnel card.
captive_bypass_body: DNS filtering and VPN DNS pause for 5 minutes so the hotel login page can load. They restore automatically.
captive_dns_bypassed: Hotel DNS in use for 5 minutes.
settings_hostname_invalid: Use 1 to 63 letters, digits or '-', not starting or ending with '-'.
settings_zone_hint: Start typing a city, for example Europe/Berlin.
settings_zone_invalid: Pick a time zone from the list.
settings_ntp: Sync the clock with time servers (NTP)
settings_ntp_servers_hint: One host name or IP address per line, up to 8.
settings_err_invalid: The router rejected a value. Check the hostname, time zone and servers.
settings_err_busy: Another change to the system configuration is in progress. Try again.
settings_err_failed: Could not save the device settings. Try again.
ssh_intro: Public keys that may log in to the router as root over SSH (dropbear). Adding or removing a key needs this browser session; API tokens cannot.
ssh_unmanaged: {count} more line(s) in authorized_keys use options or a format this page does not manage; they stay as they are.
ssh_add_label: Public key (one line from your .pub file)
ssh_remove_body: New SSH logins with this key are refused. Sessions already open stay open.
ssh_err_invalid: Paste exactly one public key line: type, key and optional comment, without options such as command=.
ssh_err_limit: The key limit (32) is reached. Remove a key first.
ssh_err_failed: Could not change the SSH keys. Try again.
reset_intro: Erases every setting and installed package and restarts the router with OpenWrt defaults. Travo is removed too unless it is part of the firmware image. Afterwards the router has no root password and LuCI answers on port 80: set a password there first.
reset_confirm_body: WiFi, VPN, AdGuard Home, saved uplinks and this interface are deleted. This cannot be undone. Download a configuration backup first if you may need it.
reset_started: Factory reset started. The router restarts with OpenWrt defaults in about a minute; this page will not come back.
reset_err_busy: Another change, restart or update is in progress. Finish it first.
reset_err_pending: A factory reset was already requested.
reset_err_session: A factory reset needs a signed-in browser session.
reset_err_failed: Could not start the factory reset.
firmware_intro: Flash an OpenWrt sysupgrade image you downloaded for this router. The image is checked first; nothing changes until you confirm. Packages you installed after the current image are dropped: to keep them, use LuCI attended sysupgrade instead.
firmware_invalid_hint: OpenWrt rejected this image. Travo never forces an image; upload the sysupgrade file for this router.
firmware_board_mismatch: Image is not for this router ({board})
firmware_packages_unknown: Packages you installed yourself cannot be listed on this router. Expect every package that is not part of the image to be gone after the flash.
firmware_packages_none: No packages were installed after the current image. Packages that are not part of the new image are still gone after the flash.
firmware_packages_dropped: {count} installed packages are not part of the current image and will be gone after the flash unless the new image includes them:
firmware_no_backup: This image cannot keep settings: the router starts with OpenWrt defaults.
firmware_wipe_warning: Without settings the router starts with OpenWrt defaults: no root password, LuCI on port 80, and Travo removed.
firmware_confirm_keep: The router writes the image and restarts; this takes several minutes. Do not power it off. Settings and Travo are kept; dropped packages are not.
firmware_confirm_wipe: The router writes the image and restarts with OpenWrt defaults; Travo and every setting are erased. Do not power it off. Download a configuration backup first.
firmware_started: Firmware upgrade started. Do not power off the router. It restarts in a few minutes; then sign in again and check the version.
firmware_err_too_large: The image is larger than 64 MiB.
firmware_err_no_room: Not enough free memory on the router for this image.
firmware_err_pending: A firmware upgrade was already started.
firmware_err_upload_busy: Another image is being uploaded. Wait for it to finish.
firmware_err_busy: Another change, restart or update is in progress. Finish it first.
firmware_err_not_staged: The checked image is gone. Upload it again.
firmware_err_no_backup: Settings cannot be kept with this image.
firmware_err_session: A firmware upgrade needs a signed-in browser session.
tailscale_absent_body: The Tailscale package is not installed. Installing needs an Internet connection and about 46 MB of free flash.
tailscale_login_body: Open the login page on any device and sign in to the tailnet this router should join. This page updates once the login is done.
tailscale_logout_body: The router leaves the tailnet. Tailnet names stop resolving and an exit node is no longer used.
tailscale_accept_dns_warning: Tailscale is set to manage DNS itself. Travo expects it off; log in again from here to fix it.
tailscale_exit_help: An exit node sends all Internet traffic of the router and its clients through another tailnet device.
tailscale_exit_none: No device in your tailnet offers itself as exit node.
tailscale_exit_use_body: All Internet traffic goes through that device. If it has no Internet within 20 seconds, the previous setting comes back.
tailscale_advertise_lan_help: Lets tailnet devices reach devices on this router's LAN. Approve the route in the Tailscale admin console.
tailscale_ssh_help: Allows SSH to this router from tailnet devices your tailnet policy permits.
tailscale_fw_help: LAN clients reach the tailnet only after the Tailscale firewall zone is added. You confirm the change after it is applied.
tailscale_fw_rollback_failed: Rolling back the firewall change failed. Check the router.
tailscale_fw_no_change: The firewall is already set up for Tailscale.
tailscale_fw_conflict: The firewall has its own sections with Tailscale's names; Travo left it unchanged.
tailscale_fw_failed: The firewall change failed. See the system log.
tailscale_err_offline: Tailscale installs once the router has Internet.
tailscale_err_no_space: Not enough free flash for Tailscale.
tailscale_err_failover: Failover is on and cannot share the router with Tailscale yet. Disable failover first.
tailscale_err_busy: Another Tailscale change is in progress or was interrupted. Try again.
tailscale_err_exit_unknown: That device no longer offers itself as exit node.
tailscale_err_exit_conflict: Turn off the WireGuard tunnel before using an exit node.
tailscale_err_exit_offline: No Internet through that exit node. The previous setting is back.
tailscale_err_no_lan: The LAN has no IPv4 network to share.
tailscale_err_failed: The change failed. See the system log.
logs_intro: The router's log since the last restart (kept in memory, newest first). It may show LAN addresses and device names.
alert_stale_guard: An interrupted operation ({name}) left its guard behind. The feature stays off until you retry it on its page.
alert_overlay_low: Flash storage is almost full (under 20 MB free). Settings may fail to save.
alert_persistence_degraded: Settings are kept in memory only: the flash overlay is unavailable, so every change is lost on restart.
alert_adguard_fail_open: AdGuard Home stopped answering. DNS bypasses it until you turn it back on.
alert_uplink_reconnect_exhausted: Automatic uplink reconnect gave up after 5 attempts. Reconnect on the WiFi page.
clients_intro: Devices on your network. Names you give stay on this router.
clients_unavailable: Could not read the client list.
clients_partial: Some details could not be read; the list may be incomplete.
clients_block_body: The device loses internet access. It can still open this admin page, so it can be unblocked from itself.
clients_unblock_body: The device gets internet access again.
clients_kick_body: The device is dropped from WiFi once. It can reconnect right away; block it to keep it off the internet.
clients_block_rollback_failed: Rolling back the change failed. Check the router.
clients_reserve_label: Always give this device the same address
clients_reservations_intro: DHCP reservations. A device gets its address the next time it renews its lease.
clients_reservation_remove_body: The device keeps its address until its lease ends, then gets any free one.
clients_err_invalid: Check the values and try again.
clients_err_caller: That is the device you are using.
clients_err_not_associated: The device is not connected to WiFi.
clients_err_ip_taken: That address is reserved for another device.
clients_err_shared: This reservation is shared with other devices; change it in LuCI.
clients_err_no_lan: The LAN address range is unknown.
clients_err_busy: Another change is waiting for confirmation.
clients_err_uci_busy: Another change is being saved; try again.
history_empty: No history yet. The first point appears within {minutes} minutes.
history_degraded: The history file was unreadable or could not be written. History is kept in memory only until you reset it.
history_reset_body: This discards all recorded traffic, client and uptime history and its file. Saving resumes afterwards.
osupdate_intro: Checks downloads.openwrt.org for newer releases. Upgrade with LuCI attended sysupgrade to keep your packages.
osupdate_unavailable: The OpenWrt update check is unavailable
osupdate_err_offline: No Internet connection to the OpenWrt release server.
osupdate_err_failed: The update check failed. See the system log.
osupdate_packages_unread: Could not read the package lists.
osupdate_packages_none_stale: None found. The package lists may be missing after a restart: use Refresh lists and check.
osupdate_never: Not checked since the router service started.
leds_unavailable: The LEDs could not be read.
leds_none: This router reports no LEDs Travo can switch.
leds_schedule_hint: Every day, router local time. Runs from cron on the router.
leds_err_same_time: The off and on times must differ.
leds_err_failed: The LEDs could not be changed.
buttons_none: This router reports no hardware buttons.
buttons_unavailable: The buttons could not be loaded.
buttons_stock_hint: Push buttons such as reset keep their OpenWrt behaviour (reboot, factory reset, failsafe).
buttons_switch_hint: One switch position turns the action on, the other turns it off. Slide it once to see which is which.
buttons_confirm_title: Let the switch change the router?
buttons_confirm_vpn: Sliding the switch will turn the VPN tunnel on or off without asking. Turning it off sends traffic over the uplink directly unless the kill switch blocks it.
buttons_confirm_guest_wifi: Sliding the switch will turn the guest WiFi on or off without asking. Turning it off drops every guest client.
buttons_err_not_configurable: This button keeps its stock behaviour.
buttons_err_failed: The switch action could not be saved.
ipv6_intro: IPv6 on the uplinks (cable and WiFi) and for LAN devices. A change is guarded: keep it within the confirm window or it rolls back.
ipv6_confirm: The router restarts its IPv6 clients and LAN advertisements. Devices pick up the change when they renew. If the IPv4 uplink changes, the change rolls back.
ipv6_rollback_failed: Rolling back the IPv6 change failed; check the router.
ipv6_no_change: IPv6 is already in this state.
ipv6_err_foreign: IPv6 is configured in a way Travo does not edit (relay mode or a custom wwan6); use LuCI.
ipv6_err_vpn_leak: Turn the VPN tunnel off first: it carries IPv4 only, so IPv6 traffic would bypass it.
catalog_intro: Optional OpenWrt services. Install, remove and turn them on or off here; set them up in LuCI.
catalog_sqm_about: Keeps calls and games smooth while the uplink is busy.
catalog_cloudflared_about: Reaches devices behind the router through a Cloudflare tunnel.
catalog_vnstat_about: Traffic statistics per interface, kept across restarts.
catalog_watchcat_about: Restarts the router or an interface when pings fail. Stays off after installing: check its settings in LuCI, then turn it on.
catalog_speedtest_about: The speedtestcpp command-line client for speedtest.net, run over SSH.
catalog_install_confirm: Installs {packages} and uses about {size} MB of flash. Packages stay until you remove them.
catalog_remove_confirm: Stops the service and deletes its packages from flash.
catalog_off_confirm: Stops the service now and keeps it off after a restart.
catalog_err_busy: An install or removal did not finish. Run it again.
catalog_err_no_space: Not enough free flash for this service.
catalog_err_built_in: This service is part of the firmware and cannot be removed.
catalog_err_in_use: Another installed package still needs it; remove that one first.
ddns_intro: Keeps a host name pointing at the router's public address through ddns-scripts. Behind a hotel or carrier NAT the address belongs to the network, not the router.
ddns_install_note: Needs Internet and about 1 MB of flash.
ddns_username: User name (if the provider needs one)
ddns_no_change: Dynamic DNS already has these settings.
ddns_err_invalid: Check the provider, host name and token.
ddns_err_foreign: The ddns.travo section was written by someone else; use LuCI.
ddns_err_busy: A ddns-scripts install did not finish; install again.
ddns_err_offline: ddns-scripts installs once the router has Internet.
ddns_err_no_space: Not enough free flash for ddns-scripts.
doh_intro: AdGuard Home sends every lookup to this encrypted server. During a captive-portal bypass the hotel's resolvers answer instead, and if the server stops answering AdGuard is bypassed (fail open).
doh_testing: AdGuard Home is testing the server…
doh_saved: AdGuard Home now uses this server.
doh_no_change: AdGuard Home already uses this server.
doh_err_invalid: Enter an https:// address without user name, password or query.
doh_err_unreachable: AdGuard Home could not resolve through this server; nothing was changed.
doh_failed: Could not change the DNS over HTTPS server.
usage_intro: Traffic per uplink from the stats history, by day in the router's time zone. Days are kept for 93 days; the last 6 hours can be lost on a power cut.
usage_err_invalid: The budget was refused. Check the fields.
usage_err_unreadable: The budget file is unreadable. Reset it first.
usage_none: No traffic recorded in this period.
usage_budget_enabled: Warn when the budget is used up
usage_budget_note: The budget only warns (an alert at the threshold and a banner once it is used up). Nothing is cut off.
usage_reset_body: This removes the unreadable budget file. The budget is off until you save a new one.
usage_no_events: No restarts or uplink changes recorded.
usage_uptime_note: Read from the 10-minute samples: up and down times are accurate to one sample, and an outage between two samples is not seen.
alert_data_budget_warning: The data budget is almost used up.
alert_data_budget_exceeded: The data budget for this billing period is used up.
alert_firmware_upgrade_completed: The firmware upgrade finished. Features paused during the upgrade are back on.
alert_memory_low: The router is low on memory. The kernel may stop services; a reboot frees memory.
wifi_page_description: Join a network for internet, and set the networks this router broadcasts.
wifi_saved_description: Networks the router rejoins on its own, top first.
wifi_mac_description: The address the router shows to the network it joins.
topology_label: How this router connects: uplinks, router and clients
dashboard_traffic_description: Live rates of every interface, including LAN and radios.
vpn_page_description: Send LAN traffic through a VPN and set the rules for it.
vpn_import_description: Paste a WireGuard configuration from your VPN provider.
tailscale_page_description: Join this router to your tailnet: reach it from anywhere, use an exit node, share the LAN.
network_wan_description: Your wired internet connection: DHCP from a modem, a static address, or PPPoE.
network_lan_description: The router's own address and the interfaces and firewall zones behind it.
network_dhcp_description: How devices on your network get addresses and names.
network_port_forwards_description: Let devices from the uplink side reach a service on your network.
network_ipv6_description: IPv6 on the LAN and a dynamic DNS name for the router.
network_diagnostics_description: Check reachability from the router and wake devices on the LAN.
services_description: Optional features on the router. Installed services come first.
system_device_description: What this router is, its name and clock, and a backup of its settings.
system_leds_description: The LEDs and buttons this router has, and night mode.
system_updates_description: Travo updates, OpenWrt release checks and firmware upgrades.
system_reset_description: Erase all settings and start over.
vpn_tunnel_needs_profile: Import and select a profile below to turn the tunnel on.
vpn_kill_needs_tunnel: Connect the tunnel first; the kill switch only turns on while the VPN is up.
vpn_change_failed: The VPN profile was not saved.
dashboard_description: What the router is connected to right now, and how it is doing.
update_disabled_off: Update checks are not set up on this router.
update_disabled_unstable: This build ({version}) is not a release, so it does not check for updates.
wireguard_page_description: Your WireGuard profiles and the tunnel that uses one of them.
adguard_page_description: Blocks ads and trackers for every device on the LAN.
adguard_default_dns_help: Every LAN device resolves names through AdGuard Home.
adguard_about: Blocks ads and trackers for every device on the LAN.
leds_all_hint: Turn every LED off, or back to normal. Each LED below can be switched on its own.
system_access_description: Who and what can sign in: API tokens, SSH keys and the admin password.
tailscale_vpn_row: Your tailnet, exit nodes and LAN sharing.
tailscale_off_body: Tailscale {version} is installed and off. Your login is kept; switching it on rejoins your tailnet.
